A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same reduced-order Lagrangian dynamics work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–G support a reliable comparison despite repagination.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix G report original simulation results for pendulums, a rope, and a cloth, including prediction errors, ablations, and runtimes.

after.justification: The original simulation results are retained, and Table 1 adds results for a linear-reduction baseline with a latent geometric LNN.

M1.justification: The written model specification changes locally: Equation (11) moves the decoder bias outside the activation and linear mapping, while Appendix C changes GyroAI's A_l domain from symmetric to SPD matrices. The overall architecture, losses, and training approach remain intact; these corrections do not establish that implementations or training runs changed.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the unactuated and sine-tracking 2-DoF pendulum, coupled 16-DoF pendulum, 192-DoF rope, and 600-DoF cloth. The new comparator uses the existing coupled-pendulum task.

E2.justification: Section 5.2.1 and Table 1 add L-OpInf (LNN, ODE), based on Sharma et al. (2024), using linear reduction with a geometric latent LNN trained through multi-step integration. The original L-OpInf, full-order LNN, and other comparators are retained.

E3.justification: No retained experiment changes its splits, metrics, budgets, or prediction horizons. Appendix F.2.2 explicitly places the added comparator under existing settings: four-dimensional linear reduction, matched RO-LNN training hyperparameters, Euler integration, and ground-truth resets every 25 steps.

E4.justification: The SPD-layer, integration-horizon, joint-training, autoencoder, latent-dimension, energy, and runtime analyses are retained. The added Table 1 comparator expands the benchmark comparison without adding a separate ablation or robustness analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions retain mean/standard-deviation and median/quartile reporting, the two-seed best-model selection in Appendix G.1.3, and the existing trajectory and timing-run counts. The new baseline follows Table 1's existing uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds a relative position error of (2.45 ± 0.96) × 10^-1 for L-OpInf (LNN, ODE), compared with the retained RO-LNN (ODE) result of (9.39 ± 3.16) × 10^-3. Existing results and plotted findings remain unchanged apart from equivalent rounding and numerical formatting.

T1.justification: Section 2 corrects the Euler–Lagrange expression to differentiate L with respect to velocity inside the time derivative, and evaluates the tangent-reduction differential at the full trajectory rather than the reduced trajectory. Equation (11) also corrects the decoder formula underlying the projection property. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the same contributions and claims about joint nonlinear reduction, geometric parameter learning, energy preservation, interpretability, and accurate high-dimensional predictions.

C2.justification: The new baseline supplies additional evidence for the existing interpretation concerning limitations of linear reduction. The substantive explanations and qualifications about reconstruction quality, latent dimension, SPD-layer instability, and cloth extrapolation remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 5 adds a project-page pointer advertised as providing source code and video. Appendix F.2.2 documents the added baseline's projection, latent learner, matched hyperparameters, and testing procedure; existing implementation details are retained.

R1.justification: V3 adds Sharma et al. (2024) on machine-learning-enhanced Lagrangian operator inference and positions its adapted baseline against RO-LNN. The broader related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: V3 adds the ICLR 2025 publication header, shortens affiliation information, and makes localized wording, mathematical-typography, and cross-reference corrections. The section organization and overall narrative are retained.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains a comparator column and more compact numerical formatting; Table 2's heading and Table 3's caption receive small edits. Existing figures and tables are reflowed across pages, with the graphical content retained.

improvement.justification: The matched latent-LNN baseline in Table 1 and Appendix F.2.2 strengthens the comparison between linear and nonlinear reduction. Corrected equations reduce specification errors, and the source-code pointer improves reproducibility information. These are focused gains within an otherwise largely unchanged paper.
